newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Skellerup Finance can't explain price fall.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Skellerup Finance can't explain price fall.

text.p: Skellerup Finance Ltd said on Friday in response to an inquiry by the New Zealand Stock Exchange concerning the fall in price of the company's listed bonds that it was unable to provide an explanation.
The yield on the bonds had risen to 27 percent on Thursday from 23 percent on Tuesday when the stock exchange made its inquiry.
Four local institutions hold nearly half of the NZ$77 million of bonds, the balance is held by retail investors.
The exchange's inquiry was the third in a month attempting to discover why the yield in the bonds had risen so high.
The bonds were initially issued in March 1996 with a yield of 10 percent.
Skellerup bonds were issued to part-fund the NZ$400 million leveraged buy-out of the Skellerup Group, led by Murray Bolton.
The buyout was conducted via Boston-based Maine Investements in which U.S. investment house Goldman Sachs has an 83 percent interest.
Business weekly The Independent earlier this month reported market concern about the performance of Skellerup subsidiary Levenes, Palmers' Garden World and Downer Miniing.
The Independent reported on May 2 on the sudden departure of Skellerup Finance's chief financial officer Wayne McCarthy.
After the Stock Exchange's second request it was revealed that Maine's bankers had reduced interest cover ratios for 1997 and brought forward some senior debt pre-payment requirements.
Boston told the National Business Review on April 25 that Maine reduced senior debt to $235 million from $315 million. He said then that investor concerns were "unjustified".
Despite the lising of the Skellerup does not have to, and does not, provide financial details of the group.
